name: Persian Pink
lede: Persian Pink is a strong, warm pink, one of a small family of color names built on Persia, the historical name for the land now called Iran, first recorded around 1923.

sections.title: A borrowed place name
sections.body:
Persia was the common English name for the country now called Iran until Reza Shah asked foreign governments to use Iran instead, a request most of the world followed from 1935 on [3]. Color dictionaries kept using Persian as a descriptive word for vivid, saturated hues well after that, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records Persian Pink from 1923, on plate 3, swatch H4 [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary files it as a strong purplish pink, only 1.3 units from that block's center, one of the closest matches in this whole batch, with the Munsell notation 3.3RP 6.8/12.9 [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is Hot Pink, 4.1 units away [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[hot-pink]], [[light-mallow-purple]], [[pink-orchid]] and [[pink-orchid]], at 4.1, 4.8, 5.1 and 5.1 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Persian Pink's bright magenta-leaning hue does not come within six units of any area color in our archive of 23,781 paintings, so it has no measurable presence there [2]. That is not unusual for the most saturated named pinks: a color this far from any natural pigment rarely survives as a dominant area in an oil painting [2]. Its family member [[persian-plum]], by contrast, is present in over two percent of the same archive, showing how far a single borrowed word can stretch across very different colors [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].

origin.named_after: Persia (now Iran); the specific reason for pink is undocumented
